evidence.excerpt: This study examines how packing pressure level affects the degree of crystallinity distribution and final part warpage in polyamide 6 (PA6) flat components (100 × 100 × 2 mm). Experiments were performed on a 60-tonne hydraulic injection moulding machine at packing pressures ranging from 40 to 100 MPa in steps of 20 MPa. Crystallinity was measured by DSC on specimens cut from five through-thickness positions. Warpage was quantified with a coordinate measuring machine at a 5 × 5 grid of points. Higher packing pressure increased average crystallinity from 28% to 36% but reduced warpage from 0.41 mm to 0.17 mm due to reduced volumetric shrinkage. A commercial process simulation code was used to model the crystallisation kinetics using an Avrami-type model with parameters fitted to the DSC data. Simulated crystallinity gradients matched measured gradients with a mean absolute error of 2.3 percentage points across all packing conditions.
